matchup_findings.statement: UCLA's rushing offense meets a Oregon defense it out-rates on the matchup scale (+2.41) (rush success rate, opponent-adjusted: UCLA offense #1 of 138, Oregon defense #47 of 138).
UCLA holds the early-down edge: its offense stays ahead of the chains on 1st and 2nd down against this defense (+0.79) more than Oregon does (-0.84).
Each offense meets a defense it out-scores on opponent-adjusted points (Oregon +0.96, UCLA +1.46).
UCLA's sustained-efficiency edge is real but not decisive (1.16, below the 2.0 strong threshold): enough for the trailing side to stay in range.
UCLA's offense has swung widely from game to game relative to its opponents (game-to-game residual variation in the 94th percentile of FBS).
Oregon's leading passer in its last game (Dylan Raiola) is not its season leader (Dante Moore): season passing numbers may not describe the quarterback who plays.

pace.definition: possession_environment = (z of home offense plays + z of away defense plays allowed + z of away offense plays + z of home defense plays allowed) / 2, on adjusted values. Positive = more snaps than an average FBS game. tempo_environment = -(z of each offense's possession seconds per play) / 2

volatility.definition: offense_ypp_residual_sd = game-to-game spread of the offense's yards per play around what the fit expected against each opponent; its percentile is within the FBS universe. explosive_yard_share_z is the raw share standardised across FBS (not opponent-adjusted). takeaways_per_game_z and giveaways_per_game_z are RAW per-game turnover counts standardised across FBS: turnovers are regression-prone and are deliberately not opponent-adjusted.
